findings.headline: Keep useContextUnsafe optional: useContext(Context) now throws outside a Provider instead of returning undefined.
findings.why: Context is created without a default, and useContextUnsafe returns useContext(Context) as is, and createContextProviderAndHook() returns it beside useContextOrThrow, which throws when the context is missing, so it is the variant that returns undefined outside a Provider, so code outside a Provider relies on getting undefined. Solid 1.x returned undefined from useContext outside a Provider; Solid 2.0.3 throws ContextNotFoundError instead.
findings.guidance: Give the context an explicit empty value, createContext<T | null>(null), and map it back in the hook: return useContext(Context) ?? undefined, so callers keep their contract. undefined is never a context value in Solid 2, so createContext<T | undefined>(undefined) still throws. If every caller is always inside a Provider, drop undefined from the hook's type instead.

findings.headline: Drop the undefined check on line 39; useContext(Context) now throws without a Provider.
findings.why: Context is created without a default. Solid 1.x returned undefined from useContext outside a Provider; Solid 2.0.3 types the result as the context's type and throws ContextNotFoundError instead.
findings.guidance: Delete the check and return the useContext result directly; the hook only existed to narrow the type. If many callers use the hook, keeping it as a one-line alias is fine.
